messages:
sam_support: Customer (AcmePay) reporting structured JSON mode over streaming keeps getting cut mid-object. Parser error: 'unexpected end of JSON input'. They pasted curl output — looks like final '}' and trailing array bracket are missing. They say this happens ~10% of streams and it's causing downstream processing failures + billing dispute.

maya_eng: ugh. can you attach the raw stream snippet? ideally curl -N so no buffering. also which endpoint (v1/chat/stream?) and model?

sam_support: pasted minimal repro they ran: 
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -d '{"model":"open-rlm-v1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"produce json"}],"json_mode":true}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream
```
Raw tail they got: 
```
data: {"id":"resp_abc","object":"chat.completion.chunk","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"{\"order_id\":123,\"items\":[]}}"}, {"delta":{"content":"\n"}}]}
data: [DONE]
```
Notice the payload ends with an extra newline but missing final array close ']' and maybe extra brace mismatch. customer parser sees truncated JSON.

carla_sre: likely a chunk boundary/flush issue or a proxy hanging up. customer uses Cloudflare in front of our API?

sam_support: they are behind a corporate proxy + Cloudflare. also reported intermittent 502s earlier.

dinesh_runtime: we saw a similar pattern last month where a midstream connection reset left SSE frames partial. Two hypotheses: (1) upstream LB (ALB/nginx) sent FIN to client while we still had buffered chunk tail, (2) our stream framing includes incremental JSON fragments that depend on client's reassembly — if proxy rewrites or drops last TCP packet the trailing bracket can be lost.

dinesh_runtime: quick repro I just did from our lab with deliberate FIN after 250ms: the last chunk ends with '..."items":[]}' but the trailing '\n]' from server's final header write may be in next packet and gets lost on abrupt close. parser fails.

maya_eng: any workaround we can give customer? they want immediate mitigation.

dinesh_runtime: tell them to retry with a client-side tolerant parser (streaming-JSON tolerant, allow trailing partial arrays and reconcile on reconnect) as a short-term. Also suggest enabling TLS keepalive and disabling aggressive proxy timeouts. On our side, we can change final SSE frame to duplicate the closing brackets in the last data frame as defensive measure. e.g. always append '\n\n}}]\n' in the final flush so partial loss less likely. Need eng-runtime signoff.

carla_sre: for Cloudflare specifically, suggest Turn Off HTTP/2 proxy buffering or increase origin response timeout, and set 'proxy_read_timeout' in nginx to >60s. Also check if their proxy sets 'Connection: close' on 204s.

sam_support: flagged as P1 by customer due to downstream pipeline breaking and billing dispute. escalation-bot: Created INC-2026-452 and assigned to eng-runtime.

dinesh_runtime: I'm going to instrument logs to capture last 3 packets for affected streams and correlate with LB logs. will add a patch to make final flush idempotent and push to canary.

maya_eng: can you drop a short repro snippet we can send to customer that doesn't require them to change infra? maybe a curl that forces smaller chunks so they see the fault locally.

dinesh_runtime: sure: 
```
# simulate early FIN (netcat used to close socket quickly)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -d '{"model":"open-rlm-v1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"json_stream_test"}],"json_mode":true,"chunk_size":64}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream | sed -n '1,80p'
# then kill the client to emulate abrupt disconnect
```
This reproduces truncated last-bracket in our env.

sam_support: noted. i'll send customer the workaround + ask them to try curl -N and increase proxy timeouts. asking billing to pause refund until we confirm root cause.

maya_eng: thanks. dinesh, if you can get a canary out with the defensive final-frame duplicate we can validate with the customer's environment. keep me posted. :thumbsup:

dinesh_runtime: will do, target canary in 2 hours. logging added: capture stream write offsets and final frame body.

sam_support: closing loop with customer now, will update INC-2026-452 with their response and attach logs when available.
